snippet.title: The Invasion | On the Edge of the Abyss
snippet.description:
The Invasion - A gripping look at the first days of WWII, revealing how a single invasion ignited a global conflict that would change history forever.

On the Edge of the Abyss – The Invasion (2019)

Director:
Writers: Nina Adler, Hendrik Behrendt
Stars: Historians, archival footage, eyewitness accounts
Genre: Documentary, History, War
Country: Germany
Language: English
Also Known As: On the Edge of the Abyss – Part 1
Release Date: 2019
Filming Location: Europe (Germany, Poland, archival sources)

Synopsis:
On September 1, 1939, German forces crossed into Poland, marking the beginning of World War II and unleashing a chain of events that would engulf the entire world. The Invasion, the first episode of On the Edge of the Abyss, reconstructs these decisive early days with remarkable precision and depth.

Through restored archival footage and expert analysis, the documentary reveals how the strategy of Blitzkrieg overwhelmed Polish defenses and shocked the international community. Political decisions, military planning, and the rapid collapse of resistance are examined to understand how quickly a regional conflict escalated into a global war.

Beyond the battlefield, the episode also captures the human dimension of the invasion — civilians caught in the chaos, soldiers facing an unprecedented form of warfare, and a world unprepared for the scale of destruction that was about to unfold.

snippet.title: October 43: The Rescue of the Danish Jews | How Denmark Defied the Nazis
snippet.description:
Title: October ’43 – The Rescue of the Danish Jews

Director: Jonatan Jerichow, Carl Otto Dethlefsen
Writers: Jonatan Jerichow, Carl Otto Dethlefsen
Stars: Survivors and witnesses of the 1943 Danish Jewish escape to Sweden
Genre: Documentary, History, War
Country: Denmark
Language: Danish (with English subtitles)
Also Known As: Jødernes flugt – vidnernes historie
Release Date: 2013
Filming Location: Denmark, Sweden

Synopsis:
In October 1943, during the Nazi occupation of Denmark, ordinary Danes united in an extraordinary act of courage — rescuing nearly 7,000 Jewish citizens from deportation by helping them escape across the Øresund Strait to neutral Sweden. Told through rare archival footage and powerful survivor testimonies, October ’43 – The Rescue of the Danish Jews reveals one of the most remarkable humanitarian efforts of World War II.

Reviews:

Written by “danishhistoryfan” on IMDb.com:
“An emotional and beautifully crafted documentary that captures both the terror and hope of 1943 Denmark. A tribute to human decency under impossible circumstances.”

snippet.title: The Deal: Trump, Bukele & the Gangs of El Salvador (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS) + El Faro
snippet.description:
What was behind Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele’s deal with President Donald Trump to imprison deportees from the U.S. at CECOT? FRONTLINE and El Faro investigate. 

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

Three months into President Donald Trump’s second term, President Nayib Bukele of El Salvador opened the doors of his country’s notorious prison, CECOT, for deportees the Trump administration had swept up and accused of being gang members. Despite revelations that most of the men had no criminal convictions in the U.S. or proven gang affiliations, as well as concerns about harsh treatment, both presidents touted the move as a win.

In “The Deal: Trump, Bukele & the Gangs of El Salvador,” FRONTLINE and reporters from the El Salvador news outlet El Faro investigate what was behind the controversial deal, and what each leader stood to gain. 

Through interviews with current and former U.S. officials, reporters and insiders, the documentary shines new light on Bukele’s tangled history with the gangs the U.S. is fighting, why Bukele offered to imprison U.S. deportees, and who he asked be returned to El Salvador from U.S. custody in exchange, in what one reporter calls “a deal within a deal.”

The Jets are looking into a pregame incident involving a Jets ball boy and Colts receiver Marvin Harrison today. Harrison was catching passes from Peyton Manning before warm-ups. Nearby, Jets punter Matt Turk was practicing and the ball boy, Matt Prior, was retrieving balls for him.

Harrison apparently became upset that the punts were sailing near him and Manning, and he confronted Prior, knocking him to the ground, according to Marty Lyons, a former Jet. Lyons, an analyst on the Jets' radio broadcast, reported that Harrison put his hands on Prior's neck before security guards ended the confrontation. The Jets confirmed that there was physical contact between Harrison and Prior and said that the league was aware of the incident.

snippet.description:
Witch Hunt in Salem - A chilling exploration of the mass hysteria that led to one of the darkest chapters in American history.

Director: Wolf Truchsess von Wetzhausen, Felicitas Hammerstein, Mariana Schneider
Writers: Not publicly available
Stars: Historical reenactments and expert analysis
Genre: Documentary, History
Country: Germany
Language: German, English, French
Also Known As: Witch Hunt in Salem
Release Date: 2017
Filming Location: United States (Massachusetts), Europe (reenactments and production)

Synopsis:
In 1692, the small Puritan town of Salem becomes the epicenter of one of the most infamous episodes of mass hysteria in history. Driven by fear, religious extremism, and social tension, neighbors turn against each other in a ruthless witch hunt that leads to the execution of innocent men and women.

At a time when Europe was beginning to move beyond the witch craze, Salem descended into chaos. Accusations spread rapidly, fueled by superstition, personal conflicts, and deep-rooted anxieties within a fragile and divided community.

This documentary explores the many theories behind the events, from psychological and social explanations to possible medical causes. It also examines the broader context of disease, war, and trauma that created the perfect conditions for paranoia to flourish.

More than three centuries later, the Salem witch trials remain a haunting reminder of how fear and belief can override reason—and how easily societies can turn against themselves.

snippet.title: President Trump’s Pressure Campaign on the Federal Reserve (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
An examination of President Donald Trump’s unprecedented attempts to assert control over the most powerful institution in the U.S. economy: the Federal Reserve.

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

“The President vs. the Fed” illuminates the roots and stakes of President Trump’s battle with Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the independence of the country’s central bank and its policy decisions.

As the documentary reports, Congress designed the Fed to be insulated from political interference so it would be free to act in the long-term interest of the economy, including by making at-times unpopular monetary policy decisions. But Trump allies argue the Fed’s independence has shielded it from accountability for its mistakes and that Trump was within his rights to try to force Powell out.

With clarity and precision, “The President vs. the Fed” examines where the battle stands now and how — with inflation on the rise amid the effects of the Iran war and Trump tariff fallout — the Fed led by Powell’s successor Kevin Warsh will likely face not only a tricky political landscape but an economic one as well.

“The President vs. the Fed” is a FRONTLINE production with Left/Right Docs. The director and correspondent is James Jacoby. The producers and writers are Anya Bourg and James Jacoby. The senior producer is Frank Koughan. The managing editor of FRONTLINE is Andrew Metz. The editor-in-chief and executive producer of FRONTLINE is Raney Aronson-Rath.

snippet.description:
Andalusia: The Legacy of the Moors - What if some of the most advanced knowledge in medieval Europe came from a forgotten empire? Andalusia: The Legacy of the Moors explores 800 years of Moorish rule in southern Spain—a time of groundbreaking science, stunning architecture, and unmatched cultural fusion. From the Alhambra to Córdoba’s Mezquita, discover how Al-Andalus shaped art, medicine, and even flamenco. Why was this legacy buried—and what remains today?

Andalusia: The Legacy of the Moors (2011)

Director: Roger Thomas
Writers: Roger Thomas
Stars: Narrated by Robert Elms
Genre: Documentary
Country: United States / Spain
Language: English
Also Known As: None
Release Date: 2011
Filming Location: Andalusia, Spain

Synopsis:
This two part series looks at the rich heritage left by the Moors who ruled southern Spain for eight centuries. Their rule was punctuated by murderous politics, constant warfare and family strife. But it produced outstanding architecture and a memorable architectural legacy – much of which still stands.
The programmes trace the achievements of Al-Andalus, concentrating on the three principal cities, Seville, Cordoba and Granada – all favourite spots for today’s tourists.
As well as the art of Islam, this insightful series, narrated by Robert Elms, touches on the scientific advances of what was briefly Europe’s most advanced civilisation.

What does it take to ensure a student graduates?
